title: Expiry: bundle lifetime during an outage, and receivers rejecting expired envelopes
summary: The rover-Gateway leg has a scheduled outage from 20 s to 50 s. During it both endpoints send short-TTL envelopes (TTL 10 s and 20 s) whose bundle lifetime, computed from the TTL per PBS-DTN-MAP-01 6.1, ends before the contact resumes, together with control envelopes (TTL 60, TTL 0 and a TTL 30 command) that outlive it. Before the outage, each endpoint offers TTL 1 and TTL 2 envelopes (too short to send; Endpoint B's TTL 2 envelope carries a Timestamp 1 ms in the past) and sends one TTL 1 envelope with a bundle lifetime override of 60 s (fault injection, not conformant to PBS-DTN-MAP-01 6.1) so that an expired envelope reaches the other receiver. TTL 3 envelopes and a TTL 2 envelope handed over at its Timestamp are sent as observations.

outages.label: rover out of view of the Gateway (planned)

criteria.text: Both endpoints refuse to send a TTL 1 envelope (lifetime bound below 1 ms after the 1 s margin)
Both endpoints refuse to send a TTL 2 envelope (lifetime bound below the 1 s ION minimum)
Receivers reject expired envelopes delivered by ION (PBS-ENV-01 12.2), including an expired command before authentication
No TTL 10 or TTL 20 envelope sent during the outage is delivered (bundle lifetime ended in storage)
TTL 60, TTL 0 and TTL 30 envelopes sent during the outage are delivered and accepted
Rover control envelopes arrive after the contact resumes (50 s + 1.55 s)
Earth control envelopes arrive after the contact resumes (50 s + 0.25 s)
At 26 s the rover node holds the 8 short-TTL rover envelopes
At 36 s the TTL 10 envelopes (bundle lifetime 8 s) are gone from the rover node
At 36 s the TTL 20 envelopes (bundle lifetime 18 s) are still held
At 46 s no short-TTL envelope is left at the rover node
At 46 s the TTL 60 and TTL 0 envelopes are still held at the rover node
At 26.4 s the Earth node holds the three TTL 10 Earth envelopes (not forwarded: no route arrives before their lifetime ends)
At 36.4 s they are gone from the Earth node
The rover node's bpstats count the short-TTL bundles as deleted at lifetime expiry
The Earth node's bpstats count the Earth short-TTL bundles as deleted at lifetime expiry
Envelopes before and after the outage are delivered and accepted
No receiver accepts an envelope older than its TTL
No duplicate or unknown envelope is received
At 26.8 s the Gateway node holds the Earth TTL 60 envelopes and the command, waiting for the rover contact
TTL 3 envelopes (bundle lifetime 1 s at A, 2 s at B) and B's TTL 2 envelope handed over at its Timestamp (lifetime 1 s); the contact plan ranges sum to 3 s (informative)

conformance.how: expired envelopes rejected by both receivers with TTL_EXPIRED (S5-3)
short-TTL envelopes not delivered after an outage longer than their lifetime; longer ones delivered (S5-4, S5-5)
TTL 0 envelopes held through the outage and delivered (S5-5, S5-12)
TTL check in receive order; discard and continue (S5-3, S5-17)
as unit tests with an injected clock (vectors RX-01 to RX-06) in both endpoints' test suites and in S7
